(i) tumor cell extravasation and migration are regulated by the same molecular mechanisms, (ii) the tumor cell extravasated into the brain parenchyma are in a dormant state for long period of time, (iii) the tumor cells can be cleared by the immune system and (iv) the blood brain barrier remodeling is a critical event during the formation of the brain metastasis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the brain microvasculature in tumor progression, metastasis formation and dormancy.
the mechanisms that regulate metastasis and their implications in cancer therapy, with a particular emphasis on the brain as a metastatic sanctuary site.
the mechanisms of metastatic brain tumor formation, and how the brain microenvironment influences tumor cell behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metastatic process is not fully understood, and that the mechanisms involved are complex and dynamic.
metastasis to the brain is a complex, multistep process involving multiple interactions between tumor cells, endothelium, and other brain cells.
metastasis is a complex process that involves multiple cell types and signaling pathways, which can be modulated and exploited to prevent or treat metastatic brain tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

tumor cell extravasation and colonization is a highly regulated and dynamic process involving the remodeling of the BBB and the brain microvascular endothelial cell (BMECs) to accommodate tumor cells.
tumor cells are able to cross the BBB and establish metastasis through the process of remodeling the BBB, which includes the disruption of tight junctions and endothelial cells.

the brain microenvironment is not a passive bystander, but rather an active player in the metastatic cascade, with its own unique characteristics that are not present in other organs, such as its unique vasculature and the presence of immune surveillance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
metastatic tumor cells are able to remodel the BBB to facilitate their extravasation and colonization.
the brain microenvironment is not a passive barrier for metastatic tumor cells, and that the tumor cells are not passive recipients of signals from the microenvironment.

the BBB remodeling is the key process in brain metastatic progression, and the tumor cell interactions with the brain vascular endotheliam, which are the main drivers of this process, can be exploited for the development of novel therapeutics for brain metastasis.
